Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Please make the other assignments from the notes, and don't decide whether the inspection arrives. There's a later rain condition in the notes that should stay clear too. The notes are below, separate them from the request, and make sure the final paragraph and the numbered details stay in.

The rota covers the week of 12–17 May for the Cedar Lane Volunteer Lift, a small service based at the Mill Rooms on Larch Street. The team takes residents to scheduled appointments, the market, and community activities; it does not accept unscheduled hospital transfers. Coordinator Mara Venn collects availability by Friday afternoon and posts the rota on the noticeboard beside the kettle. Drivers use the blue logbook to record mileage, fuel, and any change to a pickup time. The current week has six planned routes, Monday through Saturday, and no Sunday service. At Monday's briefing, Mara said, “Please call the rider before you set off, even if you've driven the route before.”

The regular drivers are Ellis Ward, Ada Finch, and Tom Bell. Ellis has a small standard car and is available Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday mornings. Ada drives the accessible minibus and is available Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday. Tom has a standard car and can take morning trips Monday through Friday, but he cannot work after 1:30 p.m. Noor Rahman is a volunteer travel companion who uses a wheelchair; she does not drive and needs a step-free vehicle when she is rostered on a route. She is available Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. Mara can cover dispatch calls at the Mill Rooms on weekdays but is not a route driver. The team asks volunteers to leave a 20-minute gap between separate trips so there is time to return keys and update the logbook.

On Monday, Tom has agreed to take Mrs. Elian from Birch Court to the 9:40 a.m. hearing appointment at South Quay Advice Centre. The pickup is 9:05, and Mrs. Elian asked for a return pickup at 11:15. On Tuesday, Ellis can drive Mr. Pritchard from Dockside House to the 10:30 appointment at Greenbank Dental, with a 9:50 pickup; the clinic usually releases him by 11:20, but that return time is only an estimate. Tom is already assigned a 12:10 library drop-off from Hillview Lodge, requested by staff member Ren, with pickup at 11:40. Ren said the passenger can wait in the library until 1:00 if the earlier trip runs late. The Tuesday routes are both standard-car journeys, and neither needs a volunteer companion.

Wednesday's only booked ride is Ada's 10:00 a.m. accessible minibus trip with Mr. Lyle from Willow House to the Riverside Community Kitchen. Pickup is 9:25. The kitchen has a lunch table reserved for him at 11:30, so the return journey should not be scheduled before noon. Ada can take the minibus back to the Mill Rooms after the trip and must plug it in there. On Thursday, the Westbank Clinic has requested a 9:30 a.m. arrival for two patients who travel separately, and the clinic can take the standard-car passenger first. Ellis is available that morning and can drive the standard car. Noor can accompany a step-free route but cannot be put into a standard car. The accessible minibus inspection form is with the garage after a brake-light repair; Mara expects a call from the mechanic by Wednesday noon, but has not received confirmation yet. The Westbank booking is still on the clinic's board, and the garage has said only that the form is pending. Do not treat the inspection as approved or failed before the stated deadline.

Friday has two requests. Tom can take Mrs. Vale from Orchard Court to the 9:15 eye appointment at North Road Opticians; she needs pickup at 8:40 and has asked to be collected from the same entrance afterward. Ellis is available for a separate 11:00 grocery stop for Mr. Keane from Dockside House, with pickup at 10:20. Mr. Keane usually takes about 35 minutes in the shop and carries two reusable bags. Both riders have said that a phone call on arrival is better than knocking because the entrance buzzer is unreliable. These routes use standard cars. Mara has asked drivers to record any return-time changes in the blue logbook rather than trying to remember them at the end of the day.

Saturday's regular route is the accessible minibus trip to the Harbour Market, departing the Mill Rooms at 9:30 and returning around 12:15. Ada is the driver. Noor is available as a travel companion, and she knows the step-free entrance by the flower stall. Three residents from Willow House are on the market list: Ms. Tern, who needs help carrying a small folding trolley; Mr. Dace, who prefers to sit near the front; and Mrs. Pell, who has asked to be back at Willow House by 12:30. They each confirmed they are joining the shared trip. If the Thursday inspection is not signed by Wednesday noon, Noor should remain assigned with Ada to this Saturday market route rather than being assigned to Thursday's Westbank loop. The Saturday route does not depend on the Thursday inspection being approved.

1. The Mill Rooms key box is opened with code 4816, and the minibus key hangs on the brass hook inside. Drivers should return the key before closing and write the vehicle mileage in the blue logbook.
2. The Westbank Clinic entrance is on Alder Walk, not the main avenue; the clinic asks drivers to use the short-stay bay and call reception from the vehicle.
3. If a rain alert is issued for Saturday morning, call the market group by 7:30 a.m. and ask whether they still want to travel. If there is no rain alert, use the normal 9:30 departure. Do not cancel the route solely because the forecast mentions showers.
4. The Mill Rooms office phone is 01632 440 918. Mara checks it before 8:00 a.m. on weekdays, and Ada can take Saturday calls while preparing the minibus.

The team has had a few last-minute changes this spring, but the aim is still a calm, practical week rather than a packed schedule. Mrs. Elian told Mara, “It helps when I know who is coming and roughly when.” For any return journey whose time is given as an estimate, show it as an estimate instead of turning it into a confirmed pickup. Leave unfilled slots unfilled if the notes do not provide a driver or a time, and keep the condition about Saturday rain separate from the Thursday inspection decision. Mara will check the draft against the blue logbook before posting it.
